title: ARMMAN's mMitra used a Google Research restless-bandit model to pick which mothers received service calls, cutting engagement drops about 30% (2021)
summary: RMAB picked weekly service calls among 23,003 mMitra mothers from 26 April 2021; 32% fewer engagement drops than standard care
account: ARMMAN's mMitra program sends automated voice messages to low-income pregnant women and new mothers in India, many of whom stop listening. With Google Research India and Harvard, ARMMAN tested a restless multi-armed bandit (RMAB) that selects which beneficiaries get limited staff service calls each week. In a seven-week field study starting 26 April 2021, 23,003 women were split into RMAB, round-robin and current-standard-of-care groups (7,668/7,668/7,667). Each week 225 RMAB-selected women were called. The RMAB group had 32.0% fewer cumulative engagement drops than standard care (p = 0.044). It had 28.3% fewer than round robin (p = 0.098, significant only at the 10% level). Round robin was not significantly better than standard care. ARMMAN reports the AI reduced drop-off risk by up to 32%. Google Research reports the system was deployed for weekly call scheduling.
purpose: Allocate limited health-worker service calls to the beneficiaries whose program engagement they are most likely to preserve.
system: Restless multi-armed bandit (Whittle index) service-call scheduler with clustering-based inference of transition parameters
developer: Google and Harvard University (Milind Tambe's group) with ARMMAN
taxonomy_note: The retained users are program beneficiaries rather than paying customers.

ratings.reason: Aggregate engagement effect; no individual health outcome documented in the field study.
The efficiency gain in call allocation is an aggregate program result.

ai_role.statement: The RMAB output chose which 225 women per week received ARMMAN-initiated service calls. ARMMAN staff blind to group made the calls. The peer-reviewed AAAI paper is by the developers with ARMMAN, so is marked vendor-authored. The non-vendor documentation is ARMMAN's own program page as the implementing non-governmental organization.
